analysis.title: Real Estate: REITs: NAREIT Management meeting takeaways: PSA, KIM, GLPI, EPRT, SAFE
key_insights: Goldman met 14 REIT management teams on Nov 17-18, 2026 at NAREIT. This note covers five: PSA, KIM, GLPI, EPRT and SAFE.

PSA: self storage demand is driven by job growth and spending. Housing is only part of it, with 15% of move-in activity from single family owners and 30% from renters. Length of stay and churn are both better y/y.

PSA is using its PS NEXT platform and data science to predict move-out probabilities. Its AI agent ELLIE will reduce call center headcount, with about $10mn of annual savings expected by 2028, roughly $0.05/share.
PSA sees Sunbelt markets as the next growth opportunity as supply headwinds decline, following the path of coastal and Midwest markets.

PSA has $791mn of acquisitions completed or committed YTD, excluding NSA and PS Canada. Mix is 54% lease-up and 46% stabilized, with 50% sourced off market. Management cites a larger acquisitions team, a cost of capital advantage as peers' financing costs rise, and data partnerships targeting micro markets.

KIM: leased occupancy ended 3Q at a record 96.6%. Anchor occupancy is still about 70bps below its all-time high. Management says fundamentals are healthy heading into 2027, credit losses are expected to stay low, and the wide signed-not-opened spread is embedded growth.

KIM says new supply is limited to outer-ring suburban pockets (Phoenix, Florida, Texas, Las Vegas) and does not compete with its first-ring product. Management estimates rents would need to rise about 45% to justify ground-up development.

KIM leasing economics have shifted toward the landlord. 83% of non-anchor leases carry 3%+ annual bumps and almost 35% carry 4%. About one-third of new anchor leases in 3Q included 2% annual escalators. In-place portfolio bumps are 1.75%-2.0% versus 1.25%-1.40% pre-pandemic.
KIM has 56 anchor boxes rolling in 2027 with no remaining options, at rents about 45-50% below market. Net effective rents are up 9% y/y. Management thinks capex-to-NOI can return to 15% or lower.
KIM margins: 51% of in-place tenants are on fixed CAM (over 70% in the legacy KIM portfolio) and about 90% of new leases include it. NOI margin has exceeded 70%.

KIM capital recycling: it sold about $150mn of flat ground leases this year and is redeploying into assets with about a 100bps initial yield spread and higher growth. About 8% of ABR remains in ground leases, enough for roughly $150mn a year of sales. Its Structured Investment Program is about $400mn against about $26bn of TEV, and management wants to grow it.

GLPI is funding an additional $60mn for Bally's Chicago at 8.5%, bringing the total commitment to $1bn. 4Q spend is expected in line with 3Q. The $940mn is to be fully funded by 1H27 when the casino opens, and the extra $60mn in 2H27.

GLPI expects most Dry Creek and Virginia Live spend in 2027. Timing for the Ione loan and LV is less certain. It sees potential for tribal deals larger than the recent ~$200mn range but remains selective.

GLPI will use debt rather than equity at its current share price and says cost of capital has not stopped it completing deals. JVs are possible only for larger deals (example given: $1bn). Management expects long-term AFFO growth of 4%, in a 2%-6% range.
EPRT has $400mn+ of LOIs at about 8% cap rates, after raising acquisition cap rates by 40bps since September. Management expects pricing to stay stable from here.

EPRT has raised $1bn of debt since 3Q26 at a blended ~4.8%, including a $500mn term loan and a convertible. The convertible's all-in cost including fees and capped call is in the mid-5% range, about 60bps cheaper than a comparable unsecured bond. No further convertible is expected soon.
EPRT estimates WACC at about 6.5%, implying investment spreads of about 150bps versus a historical average of about 200bps. It expects above-average dispositions in 2027 while equity stays expensive.

EPRT tenant health is stable with no material watchlist changes. Dave & Buster's is about 1.5% of ABR with low-2x rent coverage at acquisition. KinderCare is about $3.3mn of ABR, with coverage easing from about 2.5x to about 2.3x. EPRT has historically recovered about 80% of rent after tenant credit events.

SAFE: higher and more volatile rates have slowed transactions, including deals previously seen as highly likely to close. Sponsors struggle to secure debt and equity alongside SAFE's capital, and lender retrading continues. Rate stability matters more than lower rates.

SAFE's focus is multifamily. Affordable housing is an opportunity but small deal sizes limit earnings growth. It completed three Texas transactions this year and is targeting more states. Park Hotels and 50th Street still pay ground rent, with litigation slow and no imminent resolution.

SAFE targets 7%+ unlevered economic yields. Management's illustration of ~5% initial cash yield, ~2% annual escalators, leverage on growing rents and CPI look backs gives about 10% long-term ROE. Meaningful CPI look backs begin around 2028-2029. About 15% of the portfolio is legacy ground leases earning about 3%-3.5% versus about 6% on an inflation-adjusted economic basis.

sector_views.rationale: Company-level views only: Buy on PSA, Neutral on KIM, no stated rating in this note for GLPI, EPRT and SAFE.

earnings_insights: KIM leased occupancy was a record 96.6% at the end of 3Q, with anchor occupancy about 70bps below its all-time high.
KIM net effective rents are up 9% y/y, with NOI margin above 70%.
GLPI management expects long-term AFFO growth of 4%, in a 2% to 6% range.
PSA expects about $10mn of annual savings by 2028 from its AI agent ELLIE, roughly $0.05/share.
EPRT says 2026 and 2027 guidance carry appropriate reserves for tenant credit events.

macro_indicators.interpretation: KIM management says the national measure does not include KIM's portfolio, and its own leasing spreads remain healthy.
Discount rate in GS's Safehold price target NPV.

risk_factors: PSA: lower rental rate and occupancy growth, higher supply and competition, slower acquisition and development lease-up, higher marketing expense growth, higher cost of debt.
KIM: retailer bankruptcies in open-air retail, lower space demand, and a slower transaction market limiting capital recycling.
GLPI: weaker tenant performance, tenant bankruptcies or move-outs, and lower acquisition or development volume.
EPRT: smaller acquisition volume or spread to cost of capital, tenant bankruptcy, higher G&A, and higher rates and inflation because rents reset infrequently.
SAFE: higher interest rates, lower acquisition volume or yields, ground lease competition, tenant credit events, higher G&A and higher leverage.

tension_points.bull_case: KIM management says leasing spreads stay in today's range, with 83% of non-anchor leases at 3%+ bumps and 2027 anchor rents about 45-50% below market.
tension_points.bear_case: CoStar reports moderating national retail rent growth, though management says CoStar's measure excludes KIM's portfolio.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deterioration in the open-air retail environment with increased retailer bankruptcies, or slower improvement in occupancy and lower leasing spreads.

tension_points.bull_case: Inbound ground lease interest has improved, multifamily and new property types offer growth, and CPI look backs add earnings from 2028-2029.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher and more volatile rates have slowed transactions, and sponsors struggle to secure debt and equity, with lender retrading.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rate stability matters more than lower rates. Continued volatile rates and unavailable financing would keep conversion weak.
